name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Oral Cavity and Lip

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in South Asian populations
Increased risk in Caucasians with tobacco use

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant squamous epithelial cells with keratinization and invasive growth on biopsy
Persistent ulcerative or exophytic lesion in oral cavity or lip lasting more than 2 weeks
Radiologic evidence of local tissue invasion or bone involvement on CT or MRI
History of tobacco use, alcohol consumption, or HPV infection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant squamous cells plus compatible clinical lesion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is essential for definitive diagnosis; imaging assists in staging and treatment planning.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-healing ulcer with raised indurated margins
searchTerms: oral ulcer with raised hard edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exophytic mass with keratotic surface on lip or oral mucosa
searchTerms: raised wart-like growth on lip or mouth

common.symptomName: Persistent oral mucosal erythroplakia or leukoplakia
searchTerms: red or white patches in mouth

common.symptomName: Localized oral bleeding or blood-tinged saliva
searchTerms: bleeding or blood-tinged saliva in mouth

common.symptomName: Oral mucosal pain or tenderness on palpation

occasional.symptomName: Trismus due to tumor infiltration of masticatory muscles
Numbness or paresthesia of lower lip or chin (mental nerve neuropathy)
Weight loss due to decreased oral intake
searchTerms: weight loss due to decreased food intake
loss of appetite causing weight loss

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation between oral cavity and skin
searchTerms: abnormal connection between mouth and skin
opening draining from mouth to outside skin

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases presenting with respiratory symptoms

laboratory: Biopsy showing invasive squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls
Elevated inflammatory markers in advanced disease
imaging: CT scan showing soft tissue mass with bone erosion
MRI demonstrating local tumor extent and perineural invasion
genetic: Overexpression of EGFR in tumor cells
HPV DNA detection in subset of tumors
other: Fine needle aspiration cytology of suspicious lymph nodes

distinguishingFeatures: Slow-growing exophytic lesion with minimal cytologic atypia
Lack of significant invasion on histology
Absence of invasive malignant cells on biopsy
Mixed mucous and epidermoid cells on histology
Typically arises in salivary gland tissue rather than mucosa

redFlags: Non-healing oral ulcer persisting beyond 2 weeks
Rapidly enlarging mass in oral cavity or lip
